info.title: Vigil proxy
info.description: Vigil's own surface: the pass-through route, the feedback endpoint and Vigil's errors. Docs: https://www.vigil.wtf/docs

post.summary: Forward a POST request to the provider
post.description: A pass-through: the request is forwarded to the provider named by {provider} with {path} appended, and the provider's response comes back. Bodies are the provider's own.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The provider's own path, which may contain slashes (e.g. v1/messages).

parameters.name: X-Vigil-Key
parameters.description: Your Vigil API key. Required. Create a key in the dashboard, under Settings → API keys or on the setup page; it is shown once. On providers where the Authorization header is free, you can send it as Authorization: Bearer <key> instead. A request with no key, or a key Vigil does not recognise, is refused with 401; if Vigil cannot check the key in time, with a retryable 503.

parameters.name: X-Vigil-Agent
parameters.description: A label for the agent or app making the call. Calls are grouped by this label on the dashboard, and each label has its own optimisation settings. A call with no label, or an empty one, is untagged: it follows your account default, and the dashboard groups untagged calls by prompt.

parameters.name: X-Vigil-Optimise
parameters.description: off — run no optimisation on this request. Only the value off has an effect (it is read as a comma-separated list, so a repeated header still works). It can only switch optimisation off, never on. The call is still logged.

parameters.name: X-Vigil-Skip
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of optimisations to switch off for this request, e.g. prompt_cache. Up to 32 names, read from the first 256 characters; unknown names are ignored. Like X-Vigil-Optimise, it can only switch things off.

400.description: malformed_path, invalid_user_id, unknown_provider, missing_path, invalid_bedrock_route, invalid_vertex_route, vertex_regional_unavailable

default.description: The provider's response, passed through, with Vigil's response headers added.

x-vigil-request-id.description: The id Vigil gave this request. On every response — streamed, refused or failed. Paste it into the search on the dashboard's Calls page to find the call, what each optimisation did to it, and its saving — or why Vigil refused it.

x-vigil-techniques.description: Which optimisations ran in Shadow or On, and what each did. Non-streamed responses only. A structured-field dictionary, for example prompt_cache=on;outcome=acted. Absent when none ran.

x-vigil-saved-usd.description: The measured saving on this call, in US dollars. Non-streamed responses only. A signed decimal, negative when a cache write did not pay off. Never an estimate, and absent rather than 0 when nothing was measured. A streamed call gets only x-vigil-request-id; look its saving up by that id.

post.summary: Send a score from 1 to 5 for one of your calls
post.description: Stored under the account of the key that sends it; a later score for the same request replaces the earlier one. An unknown request id is answered exactly like a known one. At most 4,096 bytes; 1,000 a minute per key, and a daily limit per account.
